title: Your Right to Cancel an In-Home Sale
content:
# Your Right to Cancel an In-Home Sale

**Notice of the three-day cooling-off right — Window Replacement Contracts**

A sale made in the customer's home carries the federal three-day cooling-off right printed on the contract. The cooling-off right applies only to contracts whose sales channel is in-home. A cancellation qualifies for the cooling-off terms only when the customer's written notice of cancellation is given no later than the end of the cooling-off period counted from the contract signing date. Business days are counted starting the day after the contract signing date, skipping Sundays and U.S. federal holidays, so Saturdays count as business days, and notice given on the last counted business day still qualifies. Written notice is the signed Notice of Cancellation form, an email to the contract inbox or a letter, dated the day it is given or postmarked, and is recorded as a cancellation request. A qualifying cancellation carries no fee or charge of any kind, and every payment received is refunded in full, each against its own source payment, within the refund window counted in business days from receipt of the notice. Notice given after the period ends, or on a showroom or virtual consultation contract, is handled under the standard cancellation terms.

The period is the series cooling-off period in business days; the refund window is the series cooling-off refund window in business days.

## Does the cancellation qualify?

| Sales channel on the contract | Notice date (from the cancellation request) | Terms |
|---|---|---|
| In-home | On or before the last counted business day | Cooling-off: no fee or charge; every payment refunded in full |
| In-home | After the last counted business day | Standard cancellation terms |
| Showroom or virtual consultation | Any date | Standard cancellation terms |

## Counting the period (hypothetical dates)

For a 3-business-day period and a contract signed in the home on a hypothetical Thursday with no federal holiday in the following week: Friday is day 1, Saturday is day 2, Sunday is skipped and Monday is day 3. A notice dated or postmarked that Monday qualifies; a notice dated the Tuesday does not.

## Refund under a qualifying cancellation (hypothetical)

A contract with a hypothetical $2,000 deposit and a hypothetical $500 progress payment is cancelled by a qualifying notice: two refunds are issued, $2,000 against the deposit payment and $500 against the progress payment, the total being all payments received net of any earlier refunds, with no fee retained.
